sources.title: Keep a Changelog 2.0.0
sources.note: Contributed the file structure this skill prescribes: the preamble, the Unreleased section, the dated version headings, the six category names, and the reference-link block. The licence notice on the page above was read on 2026-07-30 and reads that Keep a Changelog is MIT licensed, created and maintained by Olivier Lacan.

sources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
sources.note: Contributed the bump rules for a stable release and the initial-development clause. The specification page carries a Creative Commons CC BY 3.0 notice, read on 2026-07-30, and names Tom Preston-Werner as its author.

modifications: This skill is not a fork of either specification. It carries no rule text or wording from them, prescribes their substance, links both from the body, and adds what neither states: a procedure from reading the existing changelog through handing the tag to oss-publish, the rules for which merged work becomes an entry, and a deprecation policy.

Fixed what SemVer leaves open before 1.0.0, where the specification permits anything to change. This standard uses MINOR for an incompatible change under 0.y.z, which reserves MINOR as the signal that an upgrade may break a caller, so a compatible addition takes PATCH alongside a compatible fix. The ten-row bump table states that for each case rather than leaving it to be derived.

Pinned Keep a Changelog 2.0.0 for a project that has none, and left every other convention alone. A changelog that declares a different convention, or an earlier version of this one, keeps what it declares; migrating is proposed to the maintainer as its own work rather than performed while adding an entry.

The file template reproduces the structure and the six category names as the convention defines them, with entries, versions, dates, and links written for this kit rather than taken from the upstream example file. It marks which parts are copied as they stand and which come from the repository, and it gives the GitLab forms of the compare, tag, and merge request URLs, which the upstream example does not cover.
